_readme: Routes whose owner has DECIDED to accept an unbounded chunked request body,
with the compensating control that makes it acceptable written down.
Shipped empty on purpose. iast-request-body-read-after-size-check observes
that every body-reading route buffers a whole Content-Length-less POST
before refusing it, because the checks are `if (content-length > cap)` and
1048576"> block in API-ON-DROPLET.md cannot cover that case: a chunked
request carries no Content-Length for the expression to match, so the
expression is false and the request is proxied.
Adding an entry here silences the finding for one route. That is a real
decision about a 768M-capped service on a box whose OOM killer takes MySQL
and WordPress with it, so it is written down rather than absorbed: name the
control that actually bounds it, and who decided.
The alternative fix is to read the body as a stream and abort past the cap
